claims.text: A `429 - Too Many Requests` reply (https://docs.nimbrel.example/ledger/http-status-codes) is what a Ledger node sends once it has nowhere left to put the work, which is to say once [an append queue or a read queue is full](https://docs.nimbrel.example/ledger/why-appends-are-refused).
claims.span: A `429 - Too Many Requests` reply (https://docs.nimbrel.example/ledger/http-status-codes) is what a Ledger node sends once it has nowhere left to put the work, which is to say once [an append queue or a read queue is full](https://docs.nimbrel.example/ledger/why-appends-are-refused).

claims.text: There are 3 ways an append draws a 429:
claims.span: There are 3 ways an append draws a 429:

claims.text: - The `append` or `system_append` worker pools hold more batches than they have slots for (`nbctl pool status --all`)

claims.text: - The ingest memory guard has refused the batch (`nbctl guard report ingest --counters`). [1]
claims.span: - The ingest memory guard has refused the batch (`nbctl guard report ingest --counters`). [1]

claims.span: - A circuit breaker has tripped (`nbctl breaker list --tripped`) - a breaker trips on any operation and is not particular to appends.

claims.text: A cluster that refuses appends has been given more work than its hardware can carry, so the answer is hardware: larger nodes (scale up), or more of them (scale out).
